Also, let \(\mathcal{R}^{\boldvec{j}}_{Q, \tilde{\level}}\) denote the smallest subset of
	\(\bspbasis^{\boldvec{j}}_{\tilde{\level}}\) that can be linearly combined to represent
	\(\bsp^{\boldvec{j}}_{\boldvec{i}, \level}\) on \(\meshel\).

Let us consider an active element \(\meshel \in \mesh \cap \mesh_{\tilde{\level}}\), with \(\tilde{\level}>\level\), where
	\(\thb^{\boldvec{j}}_{\boldvec{i}, \level}\) is truncated, in the sense that it vanishes on \(Q\).

issues.failure_explanation: Whether the fully truncated function (obtained by the recursion \(\trunc^{L}(\cdots(\trunc^{\level+1}(\mot)))\)) vanishes on an active element \(Q\) of level \(\tilde{\level}>\level+1\) is decided by the level-\(\tilde{\level}\) representation of the intermediate truncation \(\trunc^{\tilde{\level}-1}\circ\cdots\circ\trunc^{\level+1}(\mot)\), which differs from the mother on \(Q\subseteq\Omega_{\level+1}\): each truncation subtracts pieces supported inside \(\Omega_{\level+1}\supseteq Q\), and those pieces are generally nonzero on \(Q\). The proof instead uses the minimal set representing the mother itself on \(Q\); a level-\(\tilde{\level}\) B-spline in that set whose support sticks out of \(\Omega_{\tilde{\level}}\) may still have zero coefficient in the intermediate truncation (cancellation against the subtracted pieces), so 'the truncated function vanishes on \(Q\)' does not imply that the mother's representing B-splines are supported in \(\Omega_{\tilde{\level}}\). The implication is correct only for \(\tilde{\level}=\level+1\); the general case used in the proof is unproven, and the later step \(\mathcal{R}^{\boldvec{j}'}\subseteq\mathcal{G}^{\boldvec{j}'}\) (which concerns the mothers' representations) does not repair it.

failure_location.quote:
Since \(\thb^{\boldvec{j}}_{\boldvec{i}, \level}\) vanishes on \(\meshel\), we know that
	the support of B-splines in \(\mathcal{R}^{\boldvec{j}}_{Q, \tilde{\level}}\) is contained in
	\(\Omega_{\tilde{\level}}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the coveredness implication for the level-\(\tilde{\level}\) representation of the partially truncated function rather than the mother (e.g., via a suitable commutation property of truncation and derivation), or establish the support inclusion by a different route; if the statement fails for some knot/domain configurations, weaken it and rework lem:thb-admissibility accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The support inclusion stated in prop:thb-supp is not established; lem:thb-admissibility, whose support chain is built from this proposition, is unreliable on this ground as well (it also has an independent defect), and with it the THB admissibility-preservation claim advertised in the abstract, introduction and conclusions.
issues.title: Truncated-support proposition proved via the mother's representation, which does not control vanishing of the truncated function
issues.why_classification: The statement is a plausible local support property and only lem:thb-admissibility depends on it, so a comparable result survives; but no one-line or added-hypothesis repair exists in the source — a new, contained but nontrivial analysis of the effect of recursive truncation on elementwise representations is required.

issues.title: Downward recursion in the THB admissibility proof rests on an invalid support-domain inference
issues.why_classification: The recursion's key inference is logically false rather than a typo, and the natural single-index corrections break later steps, so the lemma needs a genuinely new but contained proof; the statement is the natural THB analog of the correctly proved lem:hb-admissibility, nothing downstream formally depends on it, and no weakening of scope is forced, so a comparable result with unchanged claim should survive without new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Then, there must be some \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{t}} \in \sideconfig_{\boldvec{i}, k}\) that
	is problematic with \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{j}}\), and \(\abs{t_k - j_k} < \abs{i_k - j_k}\).
Moreover, we say that \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{i}} \in \Bll\) is resolved in direction \(k\) if \(\sideconfig_{\boldvec{i}, k} \subseteq \Bll.\)

issues.failure_explanation: Resolution in direction \(k\) only says that the (at most two) neighbors \(\boldvec{i}\pm\boldvec{\delta}_k\) belong to \(\Bll\); it carries no information about their distance to \(\boldvec{j}\). A neighbor with \(\abs{t_k-j_k}<\abs{i_k-j_k}\) exists iff \(i_k\neq j_k\), and the case \(i_k=j_k\) is not a priori excluded by the hypotheses. It is in fact excluded — if \(i_k=j_k\), the minimal intersection forces the closed supports to intersect in direction \(k'\), and then every intermediate index on the direction-\(k'\) line has support contained in \(\overline{\supp(\xbsp_{\boldvec{i}})}\cup\overline{\supp(\xbsp_{\boldvec{j}})}\subseteq\Omega_{\level+1}\), so the direction-\(k'\) (shortest) chain exists and the pair cannot be problematic — but this argument is nowhere in the paper, so the existence step on which the recursion in lem:problematic-chain and the resolved-function skipping in alg:initiate-unchecked rely is unsupported as written (and without the observation that problematic pairs differ in all coordinates the statement would be false).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the observation that a problematic pair must differ in both coordinates (proved via the support-covering implication already used inside lem:int-box-chain's proof), and then choose the neighbor toward \(\boldvec{j}\).
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's proof has a genuine gap; the statement itself is correct once the observation is added, so the recursive use in lem:problematic-chain, the discarding of resolved functions in alg:initiate-unchecked, and the resulting exactness guarantee lem:added-1 all survive with it.
issues.title: Existence of a closer problematic neighbor asserted 'by definition' in the problematic-sides lemma
issues.why_classification: The statement is correct and the missing justification is a few lines built from an implication the paper already uses elsewhere; every dependent claim is preserved with no new machinery and no change of scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there must exist at least one pair, \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{l}},\xbsp_{\boldvec{t}} \in \chain{\boldvec{i}}{\boldvec{j}} \cap \interbox{\boldvec{i}}{\boldvec{j}}\), with a ``kink''.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in \(\interbox{\boldvec{i}}{\boldvec{j}}\) only bounds each member's index-distance to \(\boldvec{i}\) and to \(\boldvec{j}\) by \(\degree_{k'}+1\) per coordinate; two members of the box can be up to \(2(\degree_{k'}+1)-\abs{i_{k'}-j_{k'}}\) apart in direction \(k'\). Hence the kink pair (with \(l_k=t_k\)) need not have intersecting closed supports — this happens whenever \(\abs{l_{k'}-t_{k'}}>\degree_{k'}+1\), which is possible precisely in the regime where the lemma is used, since a chain contained in the box forces \(\abs{i_{k'}-j_{k'}}\le\degree_{k'}+1\). The implication 'supports intersect, hence the intermediate supports are covered by the union and lie in \(\Omega_{\level+1}\)' is the paper's own covering fact, and it is applied outside its valid range, so the kink-removal step fails for large kinks; additionally, the existence of a removable kink is only asserted ('we know that there must exist at least one pair ... with a kink') — a non-shortest chain can be kink-free whenever it contains a monotone subchain, and the case with no monotone subchain is not analyzed. The conclusion may well be true (connectivity inside the box should force a monotone chain given that same-row/column members of \(\Bll\) at distance \(\le\degree+1\) force all intermediates into \(\Bll\)), but the argument given does not prove it.

issues.why_classification: The proof contains an invalid inference plus an unproven existence claim, so it requires a new, contained combinatorial argument; the statement is expected to hold with unchanged conclusion and scope, and the repair is local to this lemma (with alg:shortest-chain, lem:containment and the algorithm's guarantee recovering once it is in place).

issues.failure_explanation: In alg:exact-mesh the variable \(\var{unchecked\_funcs}\) first appears on the left of '\(\var{unchecked\_funcs} \gets \var{unchecked\_funcs} \cup \var{corner\_func}\)' and is then used in '\(\var{unchecked\_pairs} \gets \var{combinations}(\var{unchecked\_funcs}, 2)\)', but it is never initialized in the algorithm, and alg:initiate-unchecked computes it only locally while its contract returns just \(\var{unchecked\_pairs}\). As written, the procedure references an undefined object and is not fully specified; the intended content (the unresolved functions underlying the initial pairs, augmented by the corner functions of added L-chains) must be inferred by the reader.

issues.overall_effect: The operation of the paper's central algorithm is not well-defined as written; its described five-step behaviour and the exactness guarantee addressed in lem:added-1 can only be recovered by supplying the missing initialization.
issues.title: Main exact-mesh algorithm uses the uninitialized variable unchecked_funcs
issues.why_classification: A one-line, local correction with a forced intended meaning; no change to the algorithm's logic, invariants, input-output contract, or guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\Ensure Updated truncated hierarchical basis \(\thbbasis^{\boldvec{0}}_{L}\) with no
		problematic intersections
Then the hierarchical complex \eqref{eq:hierarchical-complex} is exact for \(\level = 0, \ldots, L\).

issues.failure_explanation: The three cited lemmas only justify local ingredients (added L-chains are shortest chains; a resolved function has a problematic neighbor; a spline problematic with an added chain is problematic with one of its endpoints or its corner). The proof never argues (i) that the checking scheme cannot miss a problematic pair — skipping resolved functions in alg:initiate-unchecked is sound only after iterating lem:problematic-sides and noting that fixing the final proxy pair repairs, by prepending, the whole chain of proxies, while pairs created after each refinement are covered via lem:problematic-chain; (ii) that the while loop terminates (the marked set grows strictly and is bounded); (iii) that alg:shortest-chain is correct (which rests on lem:int-box-chain, separately defective); and (iv) that the absence of problematic intersections implies exactness — i.e., it never invokes thm:added-1, which is the actual sufficient condition for exactness. Hence the stated guarantee does not follow from what is written.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the missing correctness argument: soundness of the resolved-function skipping via iteration of lem:problematic-sides with transfer of fixes by prepending; coverage of newly created pairs via lem:problematic-chain; monotonicity of the non-problematic status under refinement; termination by boundedness of the marked set; then conclude via thm:added-1 (also repairing lem:int-box-chain, on which alg:shortest-chain rests).
issues.overall_effect: The central guarantee of the paper's algorithmic contribution ('Algorithm 1 always produces an exact mesh') is unsupported as written, and with it the exactness claims underlying the numerical examples and the abstract's promise of an algorithm-implementation framework ensuring an exact discrete subcomplex.
issues.title: One-line proof of the exact-mesh guarantee omits the completeness and termination arguments and never invokes the exactness criterion
issues.why_classification: The guarantee is expected to hold and the ingredients are present in the paper, but assembling them is a nontrivial, contained correctness argument that the proof entirely skips; the three cited lemmas alone do not establish the claim, and the exactness criterion thm:added-1 is never used, so the repair is more than routine yet requires no new global architecture and no loss of content.
